levels.official: Built into the system software by Sony.
levels.homebrew: Documented by a homebrew project (GoldHEN, etaHEN, Itemzflow). Needs that homebrew environment.
levels.experimental: Documented, but marked experimental, untested or limited to some versions.
levels.unsupported: No documented method found in the researched sources.

terms.theme: Changes the look the system offers to change: wallpaper, colours, sounds. The system home screen stays the same program.
terms.overlay: Draws extra information on top of the system or a game (FPS counter, Title ID labels, cheat menu). Nothing underneath is replaced.
terms.homebrew-app: A separate application, like Itemzflow or VantaFlow on a console, that you open from the home screen. It can look like a dashboard, but the system home screen keeps running behind it.
terms.home-redirect: A homebrew option that opens a homebrew app when the home screen would normally appear (Itemzflow 'Home_Redirection', etaHEN 'StartOption'). The system shell still runs underneath; it is not replaced.
terms.shell-replacement: Swapping the system home screen program (the shell) for another one. No documented method was found for PS4 or PS5, so VantaFlow does not claim it.

ps4-450.label: PlayStation Blog EU: PS4 system software 4.50 (custom wallpaper from screenshots)

ps4-550.label: PlayStation Blog EU: PS4 custom wallpapers via USB (5.50)

ps5-retro.label: Push Square: PS5 home screen PS1–PS4 looks for the 30th anniversary (secondary source)

ps5-retro-return.label: TweakTown: retro PS5 looks brought back (secondary source)

ps5-animated.label: OpenCritic: animated PS5 themes appearing without announcement (secondary source)

ps5-no-wallpaper.label: Addictive Tips: PS5 has no custom home-screen wallpaper (secondary source)

ps4.text: Themes and a custom wallpaper: from screenshots since system software 4.50, from images on USB since 5.50 (Settings > Themes > Custom).
Inside Itemzflow: background image, animated shader background, background music, fonts and button images through Itemzflow themes. Only Itemzflow changes; the system home screen does not.
Itemzflow downloads and shows box-art covers in its own library view.
Itemzflow coverflow library with sorting, categories and reflections, as a separate app.
Itemzflow can change an app's icon or name and hide apps by editing the system app database (app.db). VantaFlow does not do this; it changes system files.
Itemzflow 'Home_Redirection' opens Itemzflow instead of the home screen. This is a redirect, not a shell replacement.
GoldHEN overlays: FPS counter, Title ID labels and scanlines (2.3+), game SysInfo overlay (2.4b17+).
GoldHEN Cheat Menu, marked experimental in its release notes.
GoldHEN 2.4b18 known issue: Itemzflow, Apollo and Orbis Toolbox may crash the PS4 when entering or leaving rest mode.
Replacing the PS4 home screen (system shell) with another program: no documented method found.
Profile appearance was not researched for PS4 in this stage; no claim is made.

ps5.text: The home screen background follows the highlighted game; custom wallpapers are not offered (secondary sources).

Sony added PS1–PS4 style looks for the home screen in December 2024 (30th anniversary) and later brought them back; animated themes were reported in 2025 without an announcement. Availability depends on system version and rollout (secondary sources).
Profile cover image and avatar can be changed; this does not change the home screen (secondary source).
etaHEN: Title IDs on the home menu, custom debug settings text and icon, custom System Software version text.
etaHEN game overlay showing CPU, GPU, RAM and IP.
etaHEN toolbox menus and controller shortcuts, including a system-wide shortcut to open Itemzflow.
etaHEN 'StartOption' and 'launch_itemzflow' can open Itemzflow after etaHEN loads. This is a redirect, not a shell replacement.
Itemzflow runs on PS5 with its own library view; its README links a PS5 game compatibility list.
etaHEN cheats menu is marked WIP; etaHEN 2.3B toolbox support on 8.40, 8.60 and 9.xx is marked untested.
Custom home-screen wallpaper through homebrew: no documented method found.
Replacing the PS5 home screen (system shell) with another program: no documented method found.
